miway_recovery_index.source: FAO, Ontario's Public Transit Agencies (Sept 2024), Table 3.4 (CUTA Fact Book linked trips) joined to MiWay's published boardings via the 2022 overlap; derivation in docs/sources/fao-transit-2024/
miway_recovery_index.method_note: 2019=100 via the FAO/CUTA linked-trip baseline (41.2M) joined to MiWay's published boardings at the 2022 overlap (1.34 boardings per linked trip). 2019-2021 points are linked-trip ratios; 2022-2025 are boarding-equivalents. The as-published series (with its 2019 hole) is shown unchanged alongside.

service_supply.source: MiWay: TAC Service Update Nov 11 2025 p.4 (eSCRIBE 81358); TTC: Munro compilation printed segment table; TransLink: TSPR 2024. Derivation: docs/sources/miway-service-supply/
service_supply.note: The supply denominator for the recovery curves: MiWay cut hours 9% since 2019 while its peers restored or grew theirs. Ridership-per-hour is therefore up ~19% in Mississauga — crowding pressure measured, not claimed.

note: TransLink numbers come from its published stop-level APC dataset (open licence, no request). MiWay stop-level figures are the collector's observed loads — gathered by this project, not published by the agency. That difference is the data request.
trend_note: MiWay's as-published curve had to be assembled from four different document types (accessibility report, annual report, budget submission, fare strategy) across two different metrics; 2019 has no MiWay-published annual figure at all — the 2019 baseline above comes from CUTA data the FAO published, not from MiWay. TransLink's curve is one download. Both are shown as published — nothing here is modeled.
